title: Editing the Ethics of Care in Contemporary Art on Wikidata and Wikipedia: Artexte x Art & Feminism 2026 Wikiclub
content:
This year, Artexte, a library, research center, and exhibition space for contemporary art in Montreal has partnered with Art + Feminism to improve the coverage of the ethics of care in contemporary art on Wikimedia projects. The ethics of care emphasize reciprocity, interdependency, collective maintenance, and mutual support in art practices. This approach also provides an alternative perspective in contemporary art (and other sectors of society), where individual authorship and novelty are prioritized over maintenance work, such as preservation or repair.

Artists such as Mierle Laderman Ukeles have revindicated preservation, repetition, and repair as artistic practices. However, these practices often involve invisible labor that goes unseen or is undervalued, which is why focusing on care practices at the Wikiclub helps to highlight their importance in contemporary art. Care work–tasks that meet the needs of others–is also more often done by women and minorities, so highlighting it as a contribution on Wikidata and Wikipedia also helps address the gender and representation gaps on Wikimedia projects.

title: Amplifying Women’s Voice: The SheSaid Campaign in the Igbo Community
content:
The Shesaid campaign is an international campaign under the umbrella of Wiki Loves Women that focuses on the creation and improvements of entries about Women on Wikiquote. This campaign amplifies Women Voice and addresses persistent gender gap in the representation of notable women across the digital space. This year the Igbo Wikimedians User Group joins the international campaign, to address gender gap in the representation of notable women across digital platforms like Wikiquote and Wikipedia.

From 2nd September to 30th September 2026, the Igbo Wikimedia community participated in the SheSaid campaign, an initiative aimed at amplifying women’s voices and improving their representation on Wikiquote. The campaign brought contributors together to document the words, ideas, and wisdom of notable women in the Igbo language.

The campaign was organized by Akwugo, Lucy Iwuala, Sylvaline39, Ebube Clara, and Vivian Amalachukwu, who worked together to encourage participation, provide training, and support contributors throughout the campaign.

title: From Incubator to a Living Language: Ten Years of Tulu Wikipedia
content:
For a language community, a Wikipedia can be more than an encyclopedia. It can become a meeting place, a digital archive, a learning space, and a way of making a language visible on the internet. The ten-year journey of Tulu Wikipedia illustrates how a small volunteer community can gradually build a digital ecosystem for a language. or Tulu, this journey has been especially significant. Before Tulu Wikipedia became a full Wikimedia project in 2016, Tulu had only a limited presence in the digital world. Despite being spoken by a large community along the southwest coast of India called Tulunadu, the language had relatively little freely accessible digital content and few online resources through which people could learn, document and share knowledge in Tulu.

The challenge was particularly important for a language recognised by UNESCO as endangered. Digital presence can play an important role in the long-term visibility and transmission of such languages, especially as younger generations increasingly encounter knowledge through the internet.

title: From Curiosity to Contribution: My Journey with WikiSeloka
content:
I was introduced to WikiSeloka by my friend Elicefa, who is actively involved in the project of WikiSeloka. At first, I was not familiar with WikiSeloka or its activities. After learning more about it, I discovered that WikiSeloka is a collaborative initiative that aims to preserve cultural heritage by documenting and digitizing oral literature.

As someone with a strong interest in linguistics and language studies, I saw WikiSeloka as a great opportunity to learn new things. I am particularly interested in the diversity of regional languages in Indonesia, many of which reflect the rich history, values, and traditions of their communities. This interest encouraged me to join WikiSeloka, attend its weekly meetings, and take part in the project. For me, it was a chance to expand my knowledge of languages and learn how digital technology can help preserve regional languages.

title: Impact of PHP vulnerabilities on Wikimedia Cloud Services
content:
On October 20, 2026, we took Wikimedia Cloud Services (WMCS) and other services offline as a precaution due to two significant vulnerabilities that were discovered in PHP, the programming language most of our services rely on. The PHP Foundation published an advisory ahead of the announcement due to the significance of these vulnerabilities. 

Keeping the Wikimedia projects and their users secure and safe is our top priority. A significant amount of information on the Wikimedia projects is public and available for everyone, but our projects necessarily contain some personal information that is critical to keep private. Protecting user privacy is an essential part of free knowledge, and the Wikimedia Foundation Privacy Policy commits us to strive to keep non-public personal information secure.

title: Impact of PHP vulnerabilities on Wikimedia tools and services
content:
The Wikimedia Foundation is currently preparing for two critical security vulnerabilities in PHP, the programming language that underpins much of what we operate today. These vulnerabilities are severe and require affected website owners to take immediate action. This issue is not specific to the Wikimedia Foundation, but affects any website running PHP. This is a significant internet security vulnerability that many organizations are responding to right now.

You may see outages for our wikis as we work on this, and we have deliberately taken many of our supporting services offline until they can be safely patched.

title: IMILI and Wikimedia Nigeria Partner to Advance Media and Information Literacy, Information Integrity, and Open Knowledge in Nigeria
content:
How a connection facilitated by the Wikimedia Foundation’s Advocacy team opened the door to a partnership with the International Media and Information Literacy Institute (IMILI), a UNESCO Category 2 Institute with an international mandate.

Sometimes, an important partnership begins with a simple introduction.

For Wikimedia UG Nigeria, that introduction came through Costanza Caniglia of the Wikimedia Foundation’s Advocacy team. What began as an opportunity to connect with a contact within the United Nations system gradually grew into a series of institutional engagements, new relationships, and conversations about how the Wikimedia Movement could contribute to broader efforts to improve information literacy and access to knowledge.

Those conversations eventually led to a major milestone.

title: Waali Language Goes Live on Wikipedia
content:
On Wednesday, 14th October 2026, a language spoken in the sunlit towns and villages of Ghana’s Upper West Region stepped onto the world’s digital stage. Waali has become the tenth Ghanaian language, and the sixth in the Mabia/Mole Dagbani language group supported by the Dagbani Wikimedians User Group, to be approved on Wikipedia. The approval came during the language’s incubation stage in the Wikimedia Incubator. For the Waala people, it is more than a technical decision. It is a declaration that their language, history, and identity belong in the global conversation.

Waali, also spelt Wali or Waalii, is widely spoken across the Upper West Region and in parts of the Savannah Region. Thousands of people use it every day to trade in markets, tell stories, honour traditions, and raise children. Yet for all its vitality, very little research or documentation stands behind it. A language can be alive in the mouths of its speakers and still be nearly invisible in books, databases, and the digital world

title: Lessons from Accra: Rossouw van Rooyen’s take on what the first Language Diversity Conference meant for Africa’s languages
content:
Early in the first Language Diversity Conference, Rossouw van Rooyen thought about a quote he had first heard eight years earlier.

At Wikimania 2018 in Cape Town, Daniel Bögre Udell of Wikitongues quoted Richard Henry Pratt. Pratt founded the Carlisle Indian Industrial School, a notorious US boarding school for Native American children, and summed up its mission as “kill the Indian in him, and save the man”. Seeing Daniel again in Accra set the tone for Rossouw’s weekend.

“There are languages being eradicated, there are languages being suppressed all over the world which we need to save,” he says. He adds that the work is “going to be a never-ending quest.”

The conference ran in Accra, Ghana, from 2 to 4 October 2026. It was hosted by the Wikimedia Language Diversity Hub, Wikitongues and Wikimedia UK, with the Dagbani Wikimedians User Group. 82 languages were represented in the room.

title: WikiScholar 2027: bringing young readers back to Wikipedia in the age of AI
content:
Registration for WikiScholar 2027 opened on 18 October 2026. WikiScholar is a free, annual knowledge competition for students in Grades 6–10 across Bangladesh, and its entire syllabus is a reading list of Bangla Wikipedia articles.

The competition is organised by Wikimedia Bangladesh, with support from a leading corporation in Bangladesh and the Wikimedia Foundation. Students can register at registration.wikischolar.bd until 12 December 2026.

In 2026 we ran WikiScholar as a pilot in 18 schools across Dhaka and Rajshahi divisions, reaching more than 10,000 students. This year it goes nationwide.

The country’s 64 districts are grouped into six regions, each named after a river: Padma, Teesta, Karnaphuli, Surma, Rupsha and Jamuna. Every student competes in the regional round for their own region.

There are three rounds: one online, then two held in person. All dates are provisional.

The online test has 60 multiple-choice questions in 35 minutes. Questions match the board exams in difficulty, mixing knowledge-based and analytical questions. A written question may be added, but it is marked only to break ties.

title: Event brings together experts and Wikimedians to discuss internet governance in Brazil
content: Brazil is widely recognized as having one of the populations that spends the most amount of time online, averaging over 115 hours of connectivity per week. Discussing the regulation of social media, online platforms, and artificial intelligence, technologies that increasingly shape the daily lives of Brazilians, is essential. This is particularly relevant within the context of Wikimedia Brasil’s Theory of Change (2024), which advocates for the organization to take a more active role in advocacy for broad, democratic digital rights, maintaining a stance of intentionality in defending free, collaborative projects that serve the public interest.

title: The Train the Trainers Nigeria, North-West 2025; Kano State
content: The Train the Trainers (TTT) programme is an initiative of the Wikimedia User Group Nigeria (WUGN) aimed at equipping Wikimedians with the skills and knowledge needed to train others to contribute effectively to Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects. Previous editions have been organised across different regions of Nigeria, including North-Central, South-East, and North-East, helping to expand participation in the Wikimedia movement, develop new generations of editors, and improve content coverage across Wikimedia platforms. Building on these efforts, the Train the Trainers North West Nigeria 2025 was organised to strengthen community leadership, promote knowledge sharing, and support the sustainable growth of Wikimedia communities across the region.

With the Image Carousel feature, readers browse community-uploaded images, selected by editors as relevant to specific articles. The test starts on November 20.

title: How a 139-year-old family document led to my first Wikisource edit
content:
A couple of months ago, we found a bag full of documents at my house that my maternal grandmother had left behind when she passed away. Inside were baptism keepsakes, family pictures, old birth certificates, and a mysterious white envelope, among other things.

When we opened it, we found a collection of handwritten documents from the late 19th century. At first we thought they were letters, but we quickly realized they were bureaucratic papers. Through these manuscripts, my great-great-grandfather, Norverto Clavijo, was trying to obtain a promotion in the Bolivian Army. Over the course of seven handwritten pages (passed down from generation to generation and turning 139 years old in the family this year) my great-great-grandfather managed to reach the rank of commander in the Army.

The story could have ended there, but the documents also contain signatures from people who were truly important at the time. My great-great-grandfather fought in the War of the Pacific, and the manuscripts bear the signatures of heroes from that conflict. In fact, the last document is signed by the president of the Republic himself: Gregorio Pacheco.
